title: Learning numbers, socializing, and other New Orleans bands
summary: He describes learning tunes hall to hall, relaxing after jobs, and bands he heard or played with, including the Eagle Band, Kid Ory and King Oliver.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Mr. Deer, we wish you would tell us how you men went about getting arrangements to play in your band.

Well, we used to go from hall to hall sometimes where the band would orchestra be playing and each one would take us a number that could learn and we'd finally get a number down and the next day we'll go and rehearse that same number over.
Mr. Deer, when your band got through playing, did you fellas go out and meet with some of the other bands and have a jam session or what did you do?
Oh no, we went around 101 ranks to around 25 then. We all would gather together and have a little fun, play a pool and different things.
Mr. Deer, would you tell us some of the bands that you heard while you were out listening and tell us some of the groups that you may have played with?
Well, some of those I heard was Joe Robichaud, Papa Silasin, and the Eagle Band. I played with the Eagle Band myself.
And what are they now? Kid Ory.
Kid Ory. Kid Ory. King Oliver. King Oliver. King Oliver.
All right. Was there one other one?
What about the Hot Five? No, that wasn't out there.
